title: Xinran Zhou
text: INTERDISCIPLINARY ENVIRONMENTAL RESEARCH Xinran Zhou Environmental economics · Ecosystem science · Geospatial analysis I use quantitative methods to examine environmental and economic questions in agriculture, ecosystems, and land management. Email LinkedIn ABOUT ME Background and research interests I am completing a Professional Science Master’s in Ecosystem Science & Sustainability (Carbon Management) at Colorado State University, while pursuing an M.S. in Population, Resources & Environmental Economics at Shandong University. I earned a B.A. in Economics from China University of Geosciences (Wuhan). My experience spans life cycle assessment and costing, ecosystem modeling workflows, geospatial analysis, and quantitative economics—including panel-data econometrics, evolutionary game modeling, and agricultural input–output data analysis. I am interested in the economic feasibility and environmental trade-offs of agricultural and land-management decisions across different landscapes. title: Research & Technical Experience
text: RESEARCH & TECHNICAL EXPERIENCE Research & technical experience Environmental–economic assessment, land-cover change, and quantitative analysis, alongside model testing and agricultural data work. Selected research Model testing & data work Selected research ENVIRONMENTAL ECONOMICS · LCA-LCC Environmental and economic assessment of synthetic humic substances This master’s research at Shandong University evaluates four synthetic humic substance production pathways and their modeled agricultural applications in China. It connects life cycle environmental impacts with production costs and monetized environmental externalities through a regionalized LCA-LCC framework. Conference presentation Presented at the Chinese Ecological Congress · October 2025 The assessment compares applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple production, accounting for agricultural-input substitution, regional differences, and future electricity scenarios. These comparisons examine environmental–economic trade-offs under the study’s assumptions and system boundaries. Approach: Regionalized LCA-LCC · Scenario comparison · Environmental externality valuation GEOSPATIAL ANALYSIS · ESIIL Forest cover change across Colorado’s Front Range, 2001–2021 Collaborative research through CU Boulder’s Environmental Data Science Innovation & Impact Lab (ESIIL), examining forest-cover change and land-cover transitions across Colorado’s Front Range. AGU 2026 poster Accepted for presentation The analysis combines land-cover maps, elevation data, and burned-area layers to examine where forest cover changed and how those patterns vary across the landscape. Spatial overlap with burned areas is interpreted as an association rather than a causal estimate. Approach: Land-cover transition analysis · Spatial overlay · Elevation analysis Tools: Python · Google Earth Engine ECONOMETRICS Wind power policy and corporate sustainability Panel-data analysis of 58 listed wind-power firms from 2009 to 2021, using two-way fixed effects to examine policy and corporate sustainability, with mechanism, heterogeneity, and robustness analyses. EVOLUTIONARY GAME THEORY Renewable Portfolio Standards A tripartite evolutionary game model of government, renewable-energy producers, and consumers. MATLAB simulations and sensitivity analyses examine how participant strategies evolve under alternative assumptions. APPLIED QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS Industrial natural-gas customer heterogeneity Collaborative analysis of customer value classification, using Gower dissimilarity and PAM clustering to identify patterns in mixed-type customer data. Model testing & data work MODEL TESTING · LANDENGINE MEMS Grazing Scheduler testing Technical testing during an internship with LandEngine at Colorado State University, focused on configuring grazing scenarios, running tests, and reviewing scheduler outputs. The work included site-specific input preparation, testing continuous, low-rotation, and adaptive multi-paddock scenarios, and documenting model setup and output checks. Work focus: Scenario configuration · Run testing · Output review · Documentation AGRICULTURAL DATA China-specific FABIO framework Agricultural, biomass, economic, and environmental data harmonization for a China-specific FABIO framework, including accounts and product-sector mappings covering 84 agricultural products. ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT Region-specific ESG evaluation Comparison of ESG frameworks and development of evaluation approaches incorporating local environmental and economic conditions.

title: Research Portfolio
text: SELECTED WORK & RESEARCH COMMUNICATION Research portfolio A curated look at real research questions, datasets, and analytical approaches. This page replaces the earlier illustrative sample charts with descriptions grounded in completed or ongoing projects. REMOTE SENSING & SPATIAL DATA 01 / Colorado Front Range forest change Data: NLCD land-cover maps for 2001 and 2021, burned-area datasets, and elevation models. Analysis: land-cover transitions, forest-type change, spatial overlap with burned areas, and elevation-related patterns using Python and Google Earth Engine. ~19% decrease in mapped forest cover in the team’s 2001–2021 study; an association, not a causal estimate Collaborative work through ESIIL. The presentation includes team and mentor contributions. Research figures and slide files are not republished here pending sharing review. Read the project summary ENVIRONMENTAL–ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT 02 / Synthetic humic substances for agricultural applications System: four crop-residue-derived production pathways and modeled applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple systems in China. Assessment: life cycle impacts, internal production costs, monetized environmental externalities, crop-specific substitution scenarios, and regional electricity mixes. Interpretation: results depend on pathway assumptions, crop conditions, data sources, and system boundaries. Modeled economic impacts are not direct measurements of farm profitability. Research presented in Chinese at the 2025 Chinese Ecological Congress. An English summary is provided here; complete unpublished slides and underlying tables are not public. Read the project summary MODEL WORKFLOWS & SCENARIO TESTING 03 / Grazing-management scenarios Tools: MEMS Grazing Scheduler and related model workflows, with DayCent experience from training and project work. Tasks: management scenario input preparation, run testing, output interpretation, reproducible documentation, and carbon-accounting requirement review. Scope: these were ecosystem modeling and accounting tasks, not an independently developed ranch-profitability model. Only general work descriptions are shared; private project repositories and model input files remain restricted. Read the project summary Research materials and reproducibility Publicly shareable posters, figures, and code will be linked here after author and collaborator permissions are confirmed. The earlier synthetic demonstration dataset has been removed to distinguish teaching examples from actual research outputs.
